title: Agent identity and bee spawning (scent, bee, colony)
description:
Give every coding agent a friendly identity so Beads audit trails record who made each change, and build a single mechanism for agents to spawn other agents across harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Pi).

Three orthogonal parts, sharing only a contract in @hive/shared:
- scent: identity plugins for harnesses (Claude/Codex SessionStart hooks, Pi extension). Reads env only; mints an identity when none is supplied; exports BD_ACTOR (friendly name), BR_HARNESS, BR_MODEL, BR_AGENT_NAME where the harness allows env injection; injects identity into the system prompt/context.
- bee: module + thin CLI. `bee spawn <kind> <task-id>...` creates a spawn bead; `bee status <spawn-id>` reads it. Bee kinds live in a repo-root bees.toml.
- colony: one system-wide daemon (renamed from ghost) that watches spawn beads, launches harness CLIs with identity env, respawns on crash, and reaps bees whose spawn bead is closed. Only allowed cross-package import: colony -> bee.
An agent can have an identity without being a bee, and a bee is attributed through its inherited env even without scent.

Key decisions (full rationale in the transcript record child bead):
- Identity name: 3-word adjective-adjective-noun, deterministic from session id for native sessions; minted at admission for bees. Model/effort are best-effort metadata.
- Identity resolution in scent: no HIVE_AGENT_NAME -> mint from session id; name set and HIVE_AGENT_SESSION unset -> launched by colony, adopt and bind; HIVE_AGENT_SESSION == own session -> resume/compact, keep; HIVE_AGENT_SESSION != own session -> nested child, mint fresh and set HIVE_AGENT_PARENT.
- A spawn bead represents one running bee and is distinct from the task beads it works on (linked with related deps). One spawn may carry several task beads. Labels: system, bee, agent:<kind>. br label filters are exact-match, so system:bee would NOT be hidden by --exclude-label system (verified); ordinary agent work already excludes `system` and must ignore system beads.
- bees.toml `users = [...]` is a configurable list of human names (e.g. ct); `bee spawn` fails loudly if any task is assigned to one.
- No single-instance lock for colony.
- Attribution fields: BR_HARNESS=<harness> (e.g. claude) and BR_AGENT_NAME=<bee kind> (e.g. scout), never combined.
- Launch rule: all linked tasks must be ready. A bad DAG is a mistake to fix, not to work around; blocked tasks are allowed at spawn time (deferring a DAG is essential).
- All spawning goes through colony; no direct subprocess path. A parent waiting on a queued child is informed via `bee status`, not protected from it.
- Closing a spawn bead reaps the bee (enables interactive TUI bees later). Closed linked tasks count as satisfied: the launch rule applies to the open ones, and colony reaps the spawn bead before launch only when all its tasks are closed. A bee whose task claim fails closes its own spawn bead (encoded in the bee policy prompt). Crashes respawn up to max_retries; then colony closes the spawn bead and forcefully returns the bee's claimed tasks to open, as it does when reaping. colony logs to its own log, not the bead, and emits tracked events for lifecycle actions (likely JSONL).
- colony restarts are likely (e.g. upgrades): bees run detached and survive them; colony recovers from tracked pids and/or a scan of spawn beads.
- Native subagent definitions (.codex/agents, .pi/agents, agents:sync) are dropped in favour of bees, not regenerated from bees.toml. scripts/beads-loop.ts is temporary and not a design constraint.
- Supersedes the actor policy from hv-ri0 (actor = harness name).

Ordering: spikes and the ubiquitous language first; then the colony design (hv-3x8.9.1) and the spec (hv-3x8.12), which is the living reference for all later work; then rename, shared contract, scent, bee, colony, retirement.
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] A native Claude, Codex and Pi session each records a friendly actor on br mutations (Codex via --actor guidance)
- [ ] `bee spawn` + colony run a bee end to end and attribute its br mutations to its minted identity
- [ ] scripts/beads-loop.ts and native subagent sync are removed
notes:
Design conversation recorded verbatim in hv-3x8.11 (closed record; read with br show hv-3x8.11). Second-opinion reviews by gpt-6-astra are summarised there in the assistant turns.
Aligned with hv-3x8.11 turns 3, 7, 8, 10 (claude audit): added users refusal, claim-fail/reap rules, likely colony restarts, multi-task spawns, no regenerated subagents. Open questions for ct: (1) turn 10 '3. yes i'm fine with this lock for now' answers the pool-deadlock row of turn 9, so it probably means the deadlock, not a two-colony lockfile; confirm whether colony needs a single-instance lock. (2) turn 2: ct suggested the alias under the harness field (claude:scout); the assistant proposed BR_AGENT_NAME=scout with BR_HARNESS separate and ct never confirmed. (3) Multi-task spawns: if one of several tasks is closed before launch, or its claim fails, should the whole spawn bead close?
Resolved by ct after the alignment review: (1) no single-instance lock for colony; (2) BR_AGENT_NAME=<bee kind> with BR_HARNESS=<harness>, not claude:scout; (3) a closed linked task is satisfied, not blocking, so colony must allow it; a linked task blocked after spawn is left unhandled for now (future notification hooks). Still open: a claim failing on only one of several tasks.
ct: outcome labels on closed spawn beads (outcome:exhausted|reaped|unlaunched), colony-only, so bee status reports accurately. Supersedes the earlier exclusion of outcome labels for this narrow use; UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md needs updating (respawn budget -> max_retries, closed not blocked, outcome labels).

title: Spike: br database discovery across nested worktrees and BEADS_DB policy
description:
Before bee and colony pin which Beads database a bee uses, establish how br behaves when invoked from nested Git worktrees (honeycomb creates them under .worktrees/ in this repo).

Questions:
- From a nested worktree cwd, which .beads/ does br discover: the worktree's checked-out copy or the main checkout's? Is the SQLite db shared or per worktree, and how does the Husky reconciliation (pre-commit / post-merge / post-checkout) interact?
- If a bee mutates beads from a worktree while colony reads the main checkout, when does each side see the change?
- Does forcing BEADS_DB (br honours the env var and --db) to the canonical git-root database work from a worktree, and what breaks (auto-flush to JSONL, freshness checks, --allow-stale)?
- colony is one system-wide daemon serving many repos (not started per repo): how should it address each repo's database when polling spawn beads and launching bees?
- Recommend a policy: bee caller's cwd vs BEADS_DB always = canonical git root. ct leans to the bee caller's cwd, and is open to a policy change making BEADS_DB always the canonical git root if the spike shows it is needed (hv-3x8.11 turn 7 #5).

Prior evidence: hv-mmk and hv-00n verified two-worktree reconciliation. Use disposable repos/worktrees in $TMPDIR; do not mutate this repo's tracker for experiments.

description:
# Design conversation: agent identity and bees

Verbatim user/assistant dialogue from Claude Code session `5886da0d-8ce1-4f10-9909-8d0c8543094e` (2026-10-02), extracted by Pi (deepseek-flash) with the claude-session-introspection skill from the harness dialogue log. Tool calls, thinking, system reminders and background-task notifications are excluded. Turn markers are numbered `# [n] User` / `# [n] Assistant`; `##` headings inside turns are part of the messages. Turns 12–14 include earlier, abandoned wordings of the final request and one assistant reply from that abandoned attempt; they are kept as recorded. Second opinions from gpt-6-astra are summarised in the assistant turns, not reproduced. The conversation ends at the request that created this record.

# [1] User

i need to add identity to agents, this will allow bead audit trails to track the actor making changes

if you look through /Users/ct/dev/projects/millhouse.spool/spools/harnesses/plugins/millstrand-identity/README.md i had agents build this out before in another system, but i think it was a total mess and massively over complicated

help me walk through a way we could implement this in a way harnesses can use. It almost certainly needs to be a harness hook, like a claude code sessionStart hook (codex has the same) or pi which has a lower level typescript api

this gives usually gives us the model and effort, which we can use to drive env vars (if the harness lets us, which claude and pi do), and we can also pick up any environment variables set from outside, and finally we can inject the identity into the model's system prompt (helps insure it's clear and not just normal user prompt)

there are two ways an agent is launched, one is natively, e.g the desktop apps for claude/codex, the clis directly in a tty; the second is via some automation, e.g @scripts/beads-loop.ts which can much more easily set any needed env vars

for case 2, and agent might simply recieve NAME, MODEL, EFFORT, and then set its prompt. THis means we'd want some automation to mint the friendly identity first before passing it in
for case 1, the harness hook would need to mint the friendly identity (passing in model and effort from the hook if provided) and then pass this into the system prompt (and if the harness supports it, inject these as ENV vars so the agent doesn't need to keep typing them, as BD_ACTOR sets --actor automatically for example)

thoughts, you can use claude code session hooks as an example of how we'd build this

# [1] Assistant

I agree the old plugin was over-built: about 3,000 lines, a server registration callback, run references, Git workspace gates and conformance fixtures. Most of that existed only to keep identity state. If the name is derived from the session ID instead of stored, all of that state goes away.

## The core idea

Each harness hook is a thin adapter around one shared pure function. Automation only sets env vars. The hook always does the rendering.

```
 case 2 (automation)                    case 1 (native)
 beads-loop: mintName(uuid)             nothing set
 → HIVE_AGENT_NAME etc. in child env           │
            │                                  │
            └──────────────┬───────────────────┘
                           ▼
   harness hook: payload {session_id, model, effort?} + process.env
                           │
                 resolveIdentity()   ← pure, @hive/shared
                           │
              ┌────────────┴────────────┐
              ▼                         ▼
     export env (if supported)    inject into the prompt
     BD_ACTOR, HIVE_AGENT_*       "You are amber-otter …"
```

**Precedence rules:**

| field | order |
|---|---|
| name | env `HIVE_AGENT_NAME` → `mintName(session_id)` |
| model | value the hook sees → env `HIVE_AGENT_MODEL` → `unknown` |
| effort | value the hook sees → env `HIVE_AGENT_EFFORT` → `unknown` |
| `BD_ACTOR` | env, if set explicitly → derived from the above |

`mintName(seed)` hashes the seed into an adjective-noun pair from a word list. Because it's deterministic, resume, clear and compact all produce the same name again. That means no state file, no registry, and the hook can run as often as the harness likes.

## What each harness can do

| | Claude Code | Codex | Pi |
|---|---|---|---|
| hook | `SessionStart` command | `SessionStart` command | extension: `session_start` and `before_agent_start` |
| model | `model` in the payload | `model` in the payload ✓ | `ctx.model` |
| effort | ⚠️ probably not in the payload (needs checking) | ✗ not in the input schema | thinking level ✓ |
| env injection | `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` ✓ | ✗ (case 2 only, through inherited env) | change `process.env` ✓ |
| prompt | `additionalContext` (arrives as a system reminder, not the true system prompt) | `additionalContext` → developer message | real `systemPrompt` ✓ |
| stable seed | `session_id` | `session_id` (also `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in its shells) | session ID |

I checked the Codex row against the vendored `codex-rs/hooks/src/schema.rs`. The SessionStart input only has `session_id, cwd, model, permission_mode, source`, and the output only accepts `additionalContext`.

Two gaps follow from this:
- **Codex launched natively can't set env vars.** The injected context has to tell the agent to pass `--actor <name>` on every call. When the loop launches Codex, `BD_ACTOR` is already inherited by its shells, so this is fine.
- **Claude Code's true system prompt** can only be set with `--append-system-prompt`, which automation can pass at launch. A natively launched session gets `additionalContext`, which I think is clear enough.

## Suggested layout

```
lib/shared/src/identity.ts              # mintName, resolveIdentity, toEnv, renderPrompt (pure, tested)
lib/colony/src/hooks/claude.ts          # stdin JSON → writes CLAUDE_ENV_FILE + prints additionalContext
lib/colony/src/hooks/codex.ts           # stdin JSON → prints additionalContext (adds --actor guidance)
lib/colony/src/pi/identity.ts           # Pi extension: sets env + system prompt
scripts/beads-loop.ts                   # mintName(randomUUID()) → env for the spawned process
```

`colony` ("CLI abstraction over providers") seems the natural home for the adapters. Both packages are still empty scaffolds, so nothing has to move. Each adapter would be about 20–40 lines.

## Decisions to make

1. **What `BD_ACTOR` looks like.** br stores a single string, so model and effort only reach the audit trail if they're encoded in it. Options:
   - `amber-otter`: short, but you lose model and effort.
   - `claude/opus-5-5/high/amber-otter`: greppable, readable from coarse to fine. **I'd go with this one.**
   - Name only in `BD_ACTOR`, with model and effort in `--append-notes`: noisy.

   This replaces the CLAUDE.md rule that the actor is just the harness name, so CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md need updating to match.
2. **How Claude effort is read.** The options are to verify whether the payload or env exposes it, to read `effortLevel` from the settings chain, or to accept `unknown` for native sessions. I can have this checked against the docs.
3. **Gating.** I'd drop the `.millstrand` and Git gate entirely. Then the hook works everywhere and only says something when `br` is relevant, or it can run unconditionally because it's cheap.

## Related topics, if you want me to expand
- **Subagents:** Claude Task subagents share the parent's `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, so they would inherit the parent's actor. Codex has a separate `SubagentStart` hook.
- **Plugin packaging:** shipping the hooks as Claude and Codex plugins versus listing them in repo `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json`.
- **Word-list source:** pick one existing tool, such as `unique-names-generator`, or ship about 100 words inline.

If you're happy with this, I can turn it into a bead with child beads (shared core, then the three adapters, then the loop) before building anything.

# [2] User

so effort and model are best effort metadata, i don't need them if they aren't there; that said model has a place in a bead:

```
      

<pasted_content id="20b0">
--harness <HARNESS>
          Tier 1 attribution: harness identifier (env: BR_HARNESS). Recorded only [env: BR_HARNESS=]
      --model <MODEL>
          Tier 1 attribution: model identifier (env: BR_MODEL). Recorded only [env: BR_MODEL=]
</pasted_content id="20b0">

```

so we can set thos env vars if possible.

the other thing i am considering is a registry, e.g a simple toml file that gives aliases,

```toml
[[agent]]
name = "scout"
description = "fast recon agent for finding specific parts of a codebase"
systemPrompt = "focus on readonly search as per your request"
cli = "claude"
argv = "--model haiku"

[[agent]]
name = "oracle"
description = "smart advisor agent"
systemPrompt = "utalise chepaer agents to help you explore and answer questions with thorough detail. Utalise bash but in a readonly fasion"
cli = "codex"
argv = "--model gpt-astra"
```

so this could provide additional info to an agent as well as identity depending on what was set. It wouldn't work for native spawned agents, but that is unavoidable. We would want this as a label if possible on the bead, likely more useful under the harness field, e.g `claude:scout` etc

# [2] Assistant

br already has a slot for the alias. Besides `BR_HARNESS` and `BR_MODEL` there is a third tier-1 field:

```
--agent-name <NAME>   Tier 1 attribution: agent name (env: BR_AGENT_NAME). Recorded only
```

## Where each value goes

| env | value | native | via automation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BD_ACTOR` | friendly name, e.g. `amber-otter` | minted from `session_id` | minted by the launcher |
| `BR_AGENT_NAME` | registry alias, e.g. `scout` | unset | from the registry |
| `BR_HARNESS` | `claude` / `codex` / `pi` | hard-coded in each adapter | from the registry's `cli` |
| `BR_MODEL` | model ID | from the hook payload, if present | from the registry |
| *(prompt only)* | effort | from the hook, if present | from the registry |

With these fields, `BD_ACTOR` can stay just the friendly name. That settles last turn's question about how to format the actor.

**Alias field:** I'd use `BR_AGENT_NAME=scout` and keep `BR_HARNESS=claude` unmixed, rather than `claude:scout`. Every field holds one thing. Since all of them are "recorded only", nothing filters on either form, so the choice only affects how the trail reads. If you still prefer `claude:scout`, it's a one-line change in `toEnv`.

**What each harness gets:**
- **Claude Code and Pi:** all of these env vars in both modes.
- **Codex launched natively:** none of them, because it has no way to inject env. It gets the prompt telling it to pass `--actor`, and we accept losing tier-1 attribution there.
- **Codex via automation:** inherits everything from the launcher.

## Registry: there's already one half-built

`.codex/agents/*.toml` already defines `librarian` and `reviewer` with `name`, `description`, `model`, `model_reasoning_effort` and `developer_instructions`. `agents:sync` turns them into `.pi/agents/*.md`. `scripts/beads-loop.ts:18` has a third, hard-coded registry (the `agents` Map with `lead` and `worker`, selected by `agent:` labels).

A new TOML file would be the fourth place agents are defined. I'd make it the single source:

```
.hive/agents.toml   (source of truth)
   ├─► agents:sync ─► .codex/agents/*.toml, .pi/agents/*.md   (native subagents)
   ├─► beads-loop / launcher: agent:<alias> label → cli + argv + env
   └─► hooks: HIVE_AGENT_ALIAS → systemPrompt to inject
```

Bun parses TOML natively (`Bun.TOML.parse` or a direct import), so this needs no new dependency.

## Changes to your schema

```toml
[[agent]]
name = "scout"
description = "fast recon agent for finding specific parts of a codebase"
systemPrompt = "focus on readonly search as per your request"
cli = "claude"
model = "haiku"          # structured, so it can feed BR_MODEL and native sync
effort = "low"           # optional
args = ["--foo"]         # escape hatch only, and an array: no shell-splitting
```

- **`model` and `effort` as fields, not inside `argv`.** Otherwise the launcher can't set `BR_MODEL`, and sync can't emit Codex's `model` or `model_reasoning_effort`. Turning `{cli, model, effort}` into the right flags for each CLI is colony's job ("CLI abstraction over providers").
- **`args` as an array.** A string has to be split, and splitting breaks on quoted arguments.

## Who renders the alias prompt

The launcher sets env vars only: `HIVE_AGENT_NAME`, `HIVE_AGENT_ALIAS`, plus the `BR_*` and `BD_ACTOR` values. The hook looks up the alias in the registry and renders the identity and the alias's `systemPrompt` together. That gives one renderer for all three harnesses.

The trade-off is that Claude receives the alias prompt as `additionalContext` rather than as a true system prompt. The alternative is the launcher passing `--append-system-prompt` (Claude and Pi only), which splits rendering across two places. I'd keep the hook approach unless the alias prompts turn out to be weak in practice.

## Related topics, if you want me to expand
- **Codex config strictness:** whether Codex rejects unknown keys in `.codex/agents/*.toml`. This decides whether the files can be generated with extra fields or must be filtered.
- **Labels:** `agent:<alias>` labels on beads become checked against the registry instead of the Map in `beads-loop.ts`.
- **A `colony run <alias>` launcher:** a shared entry point for both `beads-loop` and ad-hoc runs.

Shall I write this up as a bead tree? Roughly: shared identity core and registry, then the three adapters, then `beads-loop` and the sync migration.

# [3] User

yes i see this as a standalone cli , that allows harnesses to spawn each other; the subagent files are a temporary solution right now, but they will be replaced by this common tool instead once it is built. I think these are two different libs; one for identity plugins, one for agent spawning. I like the bee theme, what names work? `bee spawn grunt` could simply be a wrapper around creating a bead with the correct labels, e.g a system label, the harness fields etc, then we'd need a daemon process that watches for those . colony becomes the identity lib that stores plugins for harnesses; but they should be orthoganol - you don't need colony to spawn a bee and you don't need bee for an agent to be part of the colony

thoughts

# [3] Assistant

I agree with the split. The two tools stay orthogonal if the only thing they share is a contract, meaning env var names and bead labels, and neither imports the other. Two things in the plan need adjusting first.

## Two changes to the plan

**1. Labels make the request; the `BR_*` fields only record who acted.** `--harness`, `--model` and `--agent-name` are "recorded only" and describe whoever runs that particular `br` command. If `bee spawn` set them while creating the bead, they would record the *spawner*. So the request is expressed as labels:

```
br create … --labels "system:spawn,agent:grunt"   # what the daemon acts on
```

The `BR_*` fields get filled in later, when the bee itself runs `br update --claim`.

**2. I'm reversing my earlier advice on who renders the alias prompt.** If colony's hook read the registry to inject `systemPrompt`, colony would depend on bee. Instead, bee passes the alias prompt through each harness's native flag at launch. Colony then only reads env vars (or mints a name when none are set) and injects the identity.

## Package layout

```
lib/shared     contract: HIVE_AGENT_* / BR_* names, mintName(seed)
lib/colony     identity plugins: claude / codex / pi adapters      (reads env)
lib/bee        CLI + registry + launcher + daemon                  (writes env)
```

```
bee spawn grunt ──► bead {system:spawn, agent:grunt}
                         │
               daemon (polls br ready)
                         │  look up registry → cli, model, args, systemPrompt
                         ▼
     spawn harness with env {HIVE_AGENT_NAME, BD_ACTOR, BR_HARNESS, BR_MODEL, BR_AGENT_NAME}
                         │
           colony hook installed? ── yes ─► identity in the prompt, env confirmed
                                    └─ no ──► still attributed through the inherited env
```

`mintName` goes in shared because both bee and colony mint names, which meets the "consumers clearly need it" bar.

**Where the daemon lives:** it needs the registry and the code that builds each CLI's argv. If it were `ghost`, ghost would have to import bee, which the architecture rules forbid. So either the daemon is `bee serve` inside bee, or `ghost` is folded into bee. `ghost` is currently an empty scaffold described as "the daemon process that runs it", so folding it in seems right to me.

## Names

| role | recommendation | alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| spawner CLI | **`bee`**: `bee spawn grunt`, `bee wait <id>`, `bee serve` | `queen lay grunt` (the queen lays eggs, i.e. beads), `brood`, `swarm` |
| identity lib | **`colony`**: an agent "joins the colony" | — |
| daemon | **`bee serve`** | `nurse` (nurse bees tend the brood until it hatches), if it stays its own process |
| registry | **`castes.toml`**: each entry is a caste | `agents.toml` |
| aliases | `scout`, `forager`, `guard` (reviewer), `grunt` | real worker-bee roles fit naturally |

`bee` is also the binary name of Ethersphere's Swarm node. That's niche and only matters if both end up on the same `PATH`.

## Open design points

Decided by ct (hv-3x8.11 turns 7, 8, 10):
- One system-wide daemon serving many repos, e.g. `colony wake` in a cwd containing bees.toml.
- All spawning goes through colony; no direct subprocess path. A parent waiting on a child that cannot run (pool full) is an accepted deadlock: the agent is informed via `bee status`, not protected.
- No single-instance lock (ct, after the alignment review).
- Launch rule: all linked tasks ready (not any-ready). A bad DAG is a mistake to fix; blocked tasks are allowed at spawn and simply wait.
- The spawn bead represents the running bee; if its session dies while the bead is open, colony respawns it within a budget. Crashes are expected (wrong CLI flags); colony writes clear logs to its own log, not spammed onto beads.
- Closing a spawn bead reaps its bee (enables interactive TUI bees later). Closed linked tasks count as satisfied: the launch rule applies to the open ones, and colony reaps the spawn bead before launch only when all its tasks are closed. A bee whose task claim fails closes its own spawn bead (must be encoded in the bee policy prompt).
- colony restarts are likely (upgrades): bees run detached (nohup-style) and survive; on restart colony recovers from tracked pids and/or a scan of spawn beads, live bees carry on and dead ones are replaced.
- Spawn beads are already hidden from ordinary work by --exclude-label system; no extra reservation needed.
- scripts/beads-loop.ts is temporary; do not carry its design forward.

design:
## Spawn lifecycle cases

Enumerates what colony and the bee do for each state of a spawn bead and its linked task beads. **Decided** cases come from ct (hv-3x8.11 and the notes on hv-3x8); **open** cases need a decision before implementation. A linked task counts as satisfied once closed.

### Before launch (spawn bead open, no bee running)

| # | Situation | Outcome | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Every open linked task is ready | Launch the bee | Decided |
| B2 | Some open linked task is not ready (blocked or deferred) | Keep waiting; a bad DAG is a mistake to fix, not to work around | Decided |
| B3 | Some linked tasks closed, the remaining open ones ready | Launch; closed tasks are satisfied and not handed to the bee | Decided |
| B4 | Every linked task closed | Reap: close the spawn bead unlaunched | Decided |
| B5 | Spawn bead closed (by a human or agent) | Nothing to launch; the spawn is over | Decided |
| B6 | A linked task becomes assigned to a name in bees.toml `users` after admission | Waits (not ready to the bee), launches and fails the claim, or reaps? | **Open** |
| B7 | A linked task is claimed by another agent after admission (`in_progress`, not ready) | Under B2 the spawn waits until that task closes, then B3 applies. Is waiting correct, or should colony reap/notify? | **Open** |

### While the bee runs

| # | Situation | Outcome | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Bee completes every task and closes its spawn bead | Done | Decided |
| R2 | The claim on its only task fails | Bee closes its spawn bead (encoded in the bee policy prompt) | Decided |
| R3 | The claim fails on one of several tasks | (a) work the rest, then close the spawn bead noting the failed task; (b) close the spawn bead immediately; (c) skip the task and treat it like B3 | **Open** |
| R4 | A linked task closed by someone else mid-run | Bee skips it; closed means satisfied | Decided |
| R5 | A linked task becomes blocked mid-run | Unhandled for now; future notification hooks may alert users | Decided |
| R6 | Human closes the spawn bead | Reap: colony stops the bee | Decided |
| R7 | Colony restarts | Bee keeps running detached; colony re-adopts it (mechanics to design here) | Decided |

### After the bee exits

| # | Situation | Outcome | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | Spawn bead closed by the bee | Done | Decided |
| E2 | Spawn bead open, every linked task closed | Colony closes the spawn bead | Decided |
| E3 | Spawn bead open, ready tasks remain | Respawn with the same identity within the budget; log to colony's log, not the bead | Decided |
| E4 | Spawn bead open, remaining open tasks not ready | Back to waiting under B2. Does this exit count against the respawn budget? | **Open** |
| E5 | `max_retries` exhausted | Reap: close the spawn bead and stop the bee; then tidy up as E6 | Decided (ct: spawn closed after max_retries; counting rule to design here) |
| E6 | Bee reaped, or spawn bead closed after `max_retries`, with tasks it claimed still `in_progress` | Colony tidies up forcefully: it knows the pids, the spawn bead and its task beads, so it puts each claimed task back to `open` and removes the claim | Decided |



### Outcome labels

br records no `closed_by`, so colony marks how a spawn bead ended for `bee status`. Only colony sets these, when it closes a spawn bead or notices one closed by someone else; bees never label. No label means the bee closed its own spawn bead (finished, including E2).

| Label | Case |
| --- | --- |
| `outcome:exhausted` | E5: closed after `max_retries` |
| `outcome:reaped` | B5, R6: closed by a human or agent while waiting or running |
| `outcome:unlaunched` | B4: every linked task closed before launch |

### Events

Colony emits an event for each lifecycle action (launch, respawn, reap, `max_retries` exhausted, forced claim release) so runs can be introspected and fixed later. Events are separate from the human-readable log and never written onto beads. Format to design here: most likely JSONL; SQLite only if colony grows enough to justify it (TBC).

title: honeycomb: move wk wrapper behaviour into the engine (simplify; focus follows humans, never agents)
description:
Move worktree lifecycle behaviour out of the Nushell `wk` wrapper (`lib/honeycomb/nu/honeycomb/`, ~475 lines) into the honeycomb engine, leaving the shell layer as a thin alias whose only irreducible job is changing the calling shell's cwd.

This is a simplification. `wk` works well today; the goal is to move the same behaviour into TypeScript and delete duplication, not to add new safety machinery.

## What moves

- Post-create setup and its rollback (today: wrapper runs the script, then rolls back via the `HONEYCOMB_INTERNAL_ROLLBACK` backdoor and a raw `git branch -f`).
- tmux open/switch/close and session naming (already emitted as `session.name`).
- The fzf worktree picker.
- `--self` resolution and human status lines.

The pool-full recycle picker already exists in the engine (`pickFullPoolSlot`); the wrapper only reimplemented it because it calls `--json`. The shim will call human mode, so it disappears for free.

## Focus follows the human, never the agent

One flag, `--interactive`, passed only by `wk`:

- **With it**: `add` opens and focuses the worktree's multiplexer session (or tells the shell to `cd` when not in a multiplexer); `remove`/`finish` close sessions for removed worktrees and send the shell to the canonical root if it was inside one.
- **Without it** (agents, scripts): no multiplexer calls and no cd directive at all. An agent can't steal focus or kill a session because it never touches sessions.

Terminal detection is deliberately not used: agents run inside the user's tmux panes and can have a PTY.

## Decisions

- `add` always runs setup in the engine. No deferred mode. `post_create_script_path` stays in JSON as always `null`.
- Multiplexer support is a small injected service (tmux first) so another multiplexer with a similar API could replace it.
- Shell cwd handoff: the engine writes a directory path to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`.
- `remove --self` is a boolean (the worktree containing `--cwd`).
- JSON changes are additive only.

## End state

`mod.nu` is a ~30-line shim; `tmux.nu` is deleted.

title: honeycomb: --interactive flag drives session open/close and cd directive
description:
Add the `--interactive` flag and wire the multiplexer and cd directive into `add`, `remove` and `finish`.

## Scope

- Global `--interactive` option, read after Commander parses and passed through `Deps` or dispatch.
- With `--interactive`:
  - `add`: `multiplexer.open(...)` for the new worktree; outside a multiplexer, write the worktree path to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`.
  - `remove` / `finish` cleanup: if the shell's cwd was inside the removed worktree, write the canonical root to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`; then `multiplexer.closeUnder(path)` as the **last** step, after output is written (closing the invoking session may kill this process).
- Without `--interactive`: no multiplexer calls, no cd file.
- tmux failures are a warning on stderr; they never undo the git operation.
- Git already runs from `/` (`src/git/executor.ts`), so removing the worktree containing the process cwd needs no extra handling. Verify.

## Acceptance

- Fake-multiplexer tests: interactive add opens; non-interactive add/remove make no multiplexer calls; interactive remove writes the canonical root and closes sessions last.
